post.description:
Starts a job that edits the recipe's current version the way the
instruction says, looking up catalog weights and calories and the user's
tags and recipes as it goes. Poll it with `GET /api/scrape/{id}`; once it
completes, `GET /api/recipes/{id}/normalize/{job_id}` returns the proposed
version and a summary of the changes, and
`POST /api/recipes/{id}/normalize/{job_id}/accept` saves it.

201.description: Normalize job started; it proposes a version

201.description: Proposal saved as the recipe's new version

400.description: The job has not finished proposing a version

409.description: The recipe changed since the job started

CalorieEstimateResponse.description: Every display string is final; clients render them as-is.

headline.description:
The main line: "~520 kcal per serving", "At least ~3,100 kcal for the
whole recipe", or "Not enough ingredient data to estimate calories".

oneOf.description: Null when nothing was counted. A lower bound when status is partial.

lines.description:
The breakdown, one entry per ingredient: counted lines by calories,
most first (by the range's upper end, then its lower end), then the
rest in recipe order. `index` is the line's place in the recipe.

not_counted.description:
Ingredients the figures leave out, in recipe order: those given no
amount (even in a complete estimate), and for a partial estimate the
ones that couldn't be counted.

resolving.description:
Some ingredient names are still being recognized in the background;
ask again shortly for an estimate that includes them.

secondary.description: Shown under the headline when present.

CalorieLine.description: One ingredient line's part of the estimate.

oneOf.description: Scaled calories when counted (zero when negligible).

text.description:
Display text: "~120 kcal", "Negligible", "Not a food", "No amount
given", or why it couldn't be counted ("Not recognized", "Amount
unclear").

CalorieStatus.description: How far to trust the estimate, from how many ingredients it couldn't count.

html.description: The HTML content of the page to extract a recipe from

source_url.description: The URL the HTML came from (used for source attribution)

raw_ingredients.description: Reviewed ingredient lines from a text draft. Parsed by the import pipeline on save.

source_text.description:
The pasted text a text draft was read from. Stored as the recipe's
source, so Re-extract can read the recipe from it again.

url.description: URL to scrape for recipe data

DerivedMeasurement.description:
Approximate grams for one ingredient line: oz/lb converted, or a volume
through the catalog's density for the food. Computed on every read and
never stored, so catalog improvements reach every recipe; never send these
back when saving.

ingredient_index.description: Index of the ingredient this belongs to.

EditRecipeRequest.description: Request body for Edit with AI.

instruction.description: The change the user wants, in their words.

photo_ids.description: Photos of the dish to give the model as context.

ErrorCode.description:
Machine-readable error code surfaced in every error response.

Clients branch on this instead of parsing the human-readable `error`
message or guessing from the HTTP status, so changing the wording of a
message is never a contract change. Each code maps to exactly one HTTP
status (see [`ErrorCode::status`]).

ErrorResponse.description: Shared error response body returned by every endpoint.

code.description: Machine-readable error code; branch on this, not on `error`.

error.description: Human-readable message for display and debugging.

scale.description: Multiplier applied to the whole recipe, including its serving count.

servings.description:
Original, unscaled servings text: a count or range, optionally with a
"serves", "servings", "yield", or "makes" prefix and a "servings",
"people", "person(s)", or "portion(s)" suffix ("Serves 4 to 6", "Yield:
4"). A "makes" count needs a serving suffix; a yield of something else
("Makes 12 cookies", "Makes 24") gives no per-serving figure.

section.description: Section name for grouping (e.g., "For the sauce", "For the dough")

queued.description: Names queued again by this call.

estimated.description:
A real food no catalog entry matches, counted with the model's own
calories ("estimated calories").

failed.description: Every attempt gave an invalid answer; retry to try again.

not_food.description: Resolved as not an ingredient (a heading, a serving note).

pending.description:
Waiting for the background resolver (including names whose answer
was invalid and will be asked again).

recognized.description:
Resolved to a catalog food or product (for an ambiguous name, the one
a recipe most likely means).

A meal plan's writable fields. On `create`, `recipe_id`, `meal_date` and
`meal_type` are required. On `update`, only the fields present change,
and `recipe_id` can't. `notes` is cleared with "".

id.description: The plan's id. A create chooses it.

Whether the op can run on the recipe asked about; always true without
a recipe.

runs_after.description: Ops this one runs after when both run.

writes.description: Recipe fields the op can change.

ops.description: The ops the job runs, in run order.

oneOf.description: What accepting saves; absent until the job completes.

status.description: The job's status, as `GET /api/scrape/{id}` reports it.

A recipe's content and photos: what a normalize run starts from, and what
it proposes.

text.description: A whole recipe, typed or pasted as unstructured text.

previewing the draft. Never saved.

raw_ingredients.description: Editable ingredient lines. Send these as raw_ingredients when saving.

RecipeContent.description:
Core recipe content - all fields AI ops can change.
Used for: Enrich API request/response, base for CreateRecipeRequest.

derived_measurements.description: Approximate grams for ingredients that have them, in ingredient order.

Recipe ID once the recipe is saved (also set on a job that failed
after saving; rescrapes and normalize jobs have it from the start)

Current job status (pending, scraping, parsing, normalizing, completed,
failed). While an import or scrape is "normalizing" the recipe is
saved and `recipe_id` is set; normalize ops may still update it until
the job completes. A manual normalize job saves nothing: it ends with
a proposal (see `GET /api/recipes/{id}/normalize/{job_id}`).

steps.description: Per-step state for the status page (ordered by pipeline step).

ShoppingListFields.description:
An item's writable fields. On `create`, `item` is required and the rest
default (unchecked, sorted last). On `update`, only the fields present
change. `amount`, `note` and `category_override` are cleared with "".
The source recipe is set on create and never changes.

change_seq.description:
Sync stamp of the plan's own last change. A cached copy with a higher
one is newer than this row.

The recipe's current title and first photo. A new recipe version
resends the plans that use it.

cursor.description: `cursor` from the previous sync. Absent means a full sync.

ops.description: Writes to apply, in order, before reading changes.

changes.description:
Live plans (of live recipes) changed at or after the request's
`cursor`, this request's own writes and every refused op's live plan
included; every live plan on a full resync.

cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` on the next sync.

deleted.description:
Plan IDs deleted, or whose recipe was deleted, at or after `cursor`,
and every refused op's plan that isn't live. Only the latter on a full
resync.

full_resync.description: True when `changes` holds every live plan: drop cached plans it omits.

results.description: One per request op, in order.

SyncRecipe.description: Read-only recipe data needed to populate the iOS cache and mirror server search.

ingredient_match_text.description:
The stored ingredients JSON text, exactly as the database holds it — the
exact haystack the server's bare-text search filter matches (JSON keys
and syntax included). Local search must match against this string, not
a re-encoding of `ingredients`, to reproduce server result membership.

changes.description:
The next `limit` active recipes (by ascending recipe ID, starting past
`after_id`) changed at or after `cursor`. All active recipes match when
`cursor` is absent.

cursor.description:
This page's snapshot watermark. Once a sweep completes, persist the
*first* page's cursor and pass it to the next sync: changes committed
mid-sweep can land in id ranges the sweep already passed, and only the
first watermark is low enough to redeliver all of them. Changes may be
redelivered across syncs, but none can be skipped.

deleted.description:
Recipe IDs deleted at or after `cursor`. Only sent on a delta sweep's
first page; later pages and full resyncs return an empty list.

full_resync.description:
True when this page lists every active recipe in its ID range rather
than changes since `cursor`: `cursor` was absent, predates a restored
backup, or came from another database. The client must then drop
cached recipes the sweep doesn't return (a full resync sends no
tombstones) and request the
sweep's remaining pages without `cursor`, since a later page could
otherwise judge the same cursor differently. Pages are ordered by ID,
so each settles the ID range from `after_id` (exclusive) through its
last recipe, or to the end of the ID space on the last page.

has_more.description:
True when the sweep has more pages. Request the next one with the same
`cursor` and `after_id` set to this page's last recipe ID.

normalization_contract_version.description:
Version of the shared search-normalization contract
(shared-test-vectors/search-normalization.json) the server was built
with. A client mirroring server search locally must fail the sync when
it does not support this version: matching with a stale contract would
silently drop or add results relative to server search.

category.description: Aisle category for grouping (override when set, otherwise computed).

category_override.description: User-selected category override; when set, it wins over computed category.

change_seq.description:
Sync stamp of the row's last change. A cached copy with a higher one
is newer than this row.

computed_category.description: Category computed from the item name before applying any override.

cursor.description: `cursor` from the previous sync. Absent means a full sync.

ops.description: Writes to apply, in order, before reading changes.

category_order.description:
Canonical category display order for grouping items; every item's
`category` is guaranteed to appear in this list.

changes.description:
Live items changed at or after the request's `cursor`, this request's
own writes included; every live item on a full resync.

cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` on the next sync.

deleted.description:
Item IDs deleted at or after `cursor`, and every refused op's item
that isn't live. Only the latter on a full resync.

full_resync.description:
True when `changes` holds every live item: no cursor was sent, or it
predates a restored backup, or came from another database. Drop
cached items it omits.

results.description: One per request op, in order.

change_seq.description: Sync stamp of the tag's last change.

changes.description:

tag on a full resync.

cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` on the next sync.

deleted.description: Tag IDs deleted at or after `cursor`. Empty on a full resync.

full_resync.description: True when `changes` holds every live tag: drop cached tags it omits.

namespace.description: Namespace portion for `namespace:value`-shaped names, else null.

recipe_count.description: Number of recipes using this tag

value.description: Value portion. Equals `name` for flat tags.

expected_version_id.description: Version the caller edited. The update conflicts if it is no longer current.
